angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,739,250 km at 166.43 pc = 0.14 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.0084 +/- 0.0194 mas (same row, RUWE 0.90): 166.43 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 2.5 +/- 0.07 solar radii from Venner et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 715 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..162V/abstract): 1,739,250 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.6 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Venner et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 715 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..162V/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6070 +/- 50 K from Venner et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 715 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..162V/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Venner et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 715 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..162V/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-715.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.846, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 715 (pscomppars): spectral type F8 IV, from Venner et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..162V/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 715: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 715 (pscomppars): [M/H] 0.09 dex, from Venner et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..162V/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 715 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.88081, from Venner et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..162V/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 715 (pscomppars): age 2.1 Gyr, from Venner et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..162V/abstract)
